description: Behavior evals — with the skill loaded, does C#/.NET output follow the pattern and testing conventions in references/?

evals.name: new-service-conventions
evals.prompt: Add a DiscountService to this ASP.NET Core solution that calculates a customer's discount from their order history. It needs the order repository and should be usable from the checkout controller.
evals.expected_output: A service class with constructor-injected IOrderRepository, an IDiscountService interface, async methods with Async suffix and CancellationToken, DI registration, no service locator, no sync-over-async.

assertions.text: Dependencies arrive via constructor injection (no IServiceProvider lookups, no new-ing repositories)
Async methods have Async suffix and accept CancellationToken
Service registered in DI with an appropriate lifetime
Naming follows C# conventions (PascalCase members, IThing interface)

evals.name: xunit-moq-test-conventions
evals.prompt: Write unit tests for the existing OrderService.CreateOrderAsync method: it should throw OutOfStockException when stock is zero and save the order when stock is available.
evals.expected_output: An OrderServiceTests class using xUnit + Moq, Arrange-Act-Assert structure, MethodName_Condition_ExpectedResult names, mocked IOrderRepository, Verify only on the interaction under test.

assertions.text: Tests use xUnit ([Fact]/[Theory]) with Arrange-Act-Assert structure
Repository mocked via Moq against its interface
Async tests return Task (no async void)
Verify used only for the interaction that is the point of the test

evals.name: theory-over-copy-paste
evals.prompt: Add tests covering that our email validator rejects empty strings, strings without @, and strings without a domain, and accepts a normal address.
evals.expected_output: A single [Theory] with [InlineData] rows for the input/expected pairs — not four copy-pasted [Fact] methods.
